partner_context.their_ambition: NYC Ferry already runs a six-route, ~25-landing citywide public network at a subway-equivalent fare. NYC Ferry is the citywide public ferry system run by the New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC). Launched in 2017, it carries millions of riders a year on six routes and ~25 landings linking the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island at a subway-equivalent fare.
partner_context.their_pressure: NYC's climate plan targets carbon neutrality by 2050; the ferry fleet is a diesel layer that a zero-emission foiling tier directly decarbonizes. Growth and the net-zero mandate both demand fleet renewal without disturbing the services people rely on today.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined foiling upgrade to a public ferry network NYC already runs as transit. Foiling hulls are faster and far lower-wake - valuable on the wake-sensitive, current-swept East River - and open frequencies and longer harbour hops (Rockaway, Soundview, St. George) the displacement fleet runs slowly.

hero.title: A zero-emission ferry network for New York Harbor
hero.subtitle: A foiling tier above today's ferry network on New York Harbor and the East River: faster, near-silent, low-wake lines, a clear decarbonization path, and the services people rely on left running underneath.
hero.what_we_do_together: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined foiling upgrade to a public ferry network NYC already runs as transit. Foiling hulls are faster and far lower-wake - valuable on the wake-sensitive, current-swept East River - and open frequencies and longer harbour hops (Rockaway, Soundview, St. George) the displacement fleet runs slowly.

why_now: A zero-emission foiling tier is the obvious fleet-renewal path for NYC Ferry - faster, quieter, low-wake hops on the East River and harbour, decarbonizing a system the city already subsidizes as public transit. NYC's climate plan targets carbon neutrality by 2050; the ferry fleet is a diesel layer that a zero-emission foiling tier directly decarbonizes. A demo vessel is on the water now.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the network as the fast marine mode on New York Harbor and the East River — feeding the existing rail, metro and bus interchanges and adding lines toward the authority's published growth and net-zero targets.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined and autonomy-ready — the same DNA as the autonomous road programs — built for fleet operation, with a ~100-vessel network proving the model in the Maldives.

proof_points.claim: The authority runs marine transport at public scale.
proof_points.evidence: East River, South Brooklyn, Astoria, Rockaway-Soundview, St. George and Governors Island routes - landings from Throgs Neck and Soundview in the Bronx to the Rockaways, St. George and Bay Ridge.
proof_points.source: NYC Ferry (New York City Economic Development Corporation)

proof_points.claim: There is a published growth and decarbonization mandate.
proof_points.evidence: NYC's climate plan targets carbon neutrality by 2050; the ferry fleet is a diesel layer that a zero-emission foiling tier directly decarbonizes.
proof_points.source: OneNYC / carbon-neutral 2050; citywide ferry as an equitable public transit mode

proof_points.evidence: Hydrofoiling, software-governed vessels — the same DNA arriving in autonomous road mobility — built for fleet operation.

proof_points.claim: The fleet model is real and at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing proving the network model in the Maldives; 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours; a demo vessel is on the water now.

objections.concern: Will this change the subway-equivalent public fare?
objections.response: No — Navier renews and decarbonizes the fleet on the same publicly-run, subway-fare network. It is fleet upgrade, not a fare change; the city keeps the ferry as equitable transit.
Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at existing piers — no new shore power, vertiports or rights-of-way.

objections.concern: Is foiling safe in busy, shared public waterways?
objections.response: Foiling is software-governed — geofenced no-foil and low-wake zones near piers, ferry lanes and moorings, automatic speed and wake limits in shared water, and conventional low-speed handling everywhere it isn't cleared to fly.

phases.label: Phase 1 — East River commuter pilot
phases.rationale: Start where demand is already proven — the busiest commuter corridors, upgraded to faster, zero-emission foiling vessels.
phases.narrative: A focused commuter pilot on New York Harbor and the East River — proving the foiling tier in sheltered home waters, additive to the existing ferry services, with no new charging beyond a berth pedestal.

phases.label: Phase 2 — full citywide harbour network
phases.rationale: Extend across the full New York Harbor and the East River network as the pilot proves out.
phases.narrative: Grow the foiling tier across the full New York Harbor and the East River network — faster, cleaner, low-wake service the length of the system.

phases.label: Phase 3 — Midtown & NJ Gold Coast
phases.rationale: Add the longer and busier domestic lines as ridership grows.
phases.narrative: A well-used domestic network on New York Harbor and the East River as ridership grows toward the authority's published targets.

phases.label: Phase 4 — JFK / Jamaica Bay roadmap
phases.rationale: Optional longer open-water domestic legs on the roadmap, held out of near-term numbers.
phases.narrative: Far-future domestic reach on New York Harbor and the East River, sequenced after the core network is proven.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + long-range hybrid), the Maldives-proven network playbook, certification and operations.
the_ask.partner_brings: Network integration, berth access, the published network mandate and regulatory cover.
the_ask.next_step: A East River commuter pilot, co-specified with the authority against its published network and net-zero targets.

close.title: A zero-emission water layer that grows with the city.
close.body: Start on the busiest commuter corridors, scale across the full New York Harbor and the East River network, then mature the service — a zero-emission foiling tier that advances the authority's net-zero mandate while the services people rely on keep running underneath.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop — roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — the open water and the piers already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the long-range hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. Nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the charging excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

Regional legs 75–150nm beyond Pioneer range. Held out of near-term numbers.
